title: Single-conclusion intuitionistic propositional sequents

based_on.title: Introduction to Proof Theory (OPLSS 2023 lecture notes)
based_on.pages: Sections 8 and 10, printed pp. 12–13 and 16–17 (NJ and LJ rule presentations).

based_on.title: Proof Theory: Foundations and Applications (June 2013 lecture notes)

summary: Translate finite single-conclusion sequent proofs and intuitionistic natural-deduction proofs into one another using explicit left rules and cut.
abstract: A proof can use an implication by establishing its antecedent and continuing from its consequent. Sequent rules make these two parts of the argument visible, while keeping exactly one formula as the conclusion. We define a finite intuitionistic calculus and show that it proves exactly the same formulas from the same finite assumptions as natural deduction. The translations explain how left rules use conjunctions and disjunctions, how differing assumptions combine, and why cut composes proofs through an intermediate formula. A complete worked proof illustrates the rules, and finite support connects this presentation with deductions from arbitrary sets of assumptions.
